pr_title: Fix the snapshots permissions on unix system
pr_body:
# Pull Request

## Related issue
Fixes https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/issues/3507

The snapshot permissions were wrong after the v0.30 and the huge refacto of the index scheduler.
Fix this issue + add a test on the permissions on unix

issue_context.title: Snapshot file permission issues
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
After creating a snapshot, data.ms.snapshot file has incorrect permissions, unable to interact with it without sudo or as root

**To Reproduce**
`docker run -e MEILI_SNAPSHOT_DIR="/snapshots" -e MEILI_SCHEDULE_SNAPSHOT=true -e MEILI_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_SEC=10 getmeili/meilisearch:v0.29.0`
The snapshot in /snapshots folder has correct permissions (see screenshots)

`docker run -e MEILI_SNAPSHOT_DIR="/snapshots" -e MEILI_SCHEDULE_SNAPSHOT=true -e MEILI_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_SEC=10 getmeili/meilisearch:v0.30.0`
The snapshot in /snapshots folder has incorrect permissions (see screenshots)

**Screenshots**
Using v0.29.0
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/118532529/219595612-64262ae8-df76-4e10-ab46-175e66ca5ba0.png)
Using v0.30.0-v1.0.0
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/118532529/219598028-3f7225bf-df43-4a86-8cd7-d3d4168ffd95.png)


**Meilisearch version:** v0.29.0, v0.30.0-v1.0.0
comments: Hello @Magorx15. Thank you for informing us about this problem. Indeed the snapshot permission file changed from v0.30 upward. I'm not sure if this change was intended or not; however, I'd discuss it with the team and get back to you. I understand this might trigger permission issues, but I would like to know specifically how this change impacts you. Thanks again.
We are trying to upload the snapshot to somewhere else (and therefore we need read permission) which obviously fails as it needs root user for that

Hey @Magorx15, yeah, this was definitely an issue on our side; it should be fixed for the next release!

First RCs coming this week, and official release will be 3rd April!

Thanks for the report 💯
Fixed by #3561, will be released in v1.1.0-rc.1 by the end of the week or at the beginning of next week

review_comments: What is the mode set by`set_readonly`? not sure to understand what they meant by readonly.

From what I see, it removes the right to write + sets the right to read if you're root.

_I think_ it's sufficient for windows, but it's not for UNIX. I decided to keep it just in case, but tbh, I don't really know if we should.
Thank you! It looks like you are right. We must set the read bits to true for the root part.
